# Detecting viruses and antiviral targets

> *Viruses are too small for the light microscope and grow only in living cells, so they are usually detected by their nucleic acid, their proteins or the antibodies they provoke.*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The plan for this chapter:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| Learning objectives | Choose between nucleic acid tests, antigen tests and serology for a question about a viral infection; name the steps of the replication cycle that drugs block |
| Detection | NAATs, antigen tests, serology (IgM and paired sera), with what each result means; cell culture in reference laboratories |
| Antiviral targets | A flow of the replication cycle marked with the steps drugs act on; why there are fewer antiviral than antibacterial drugs |
| Scenario questions | Which test best answers a described clinical question |
